# dtcloud_lb_health_monitor (Resource)

Manages the health check attached to a pool, which decides whether a member still receives traffic.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "dtcloud_lb_health_monitor" "web" {
  lb_id   = dtcloud_lb.public.id
  pool_id = dtcloud_lb_pool.web.pool_id

  # A pool can carry only one monitor; a second one is refused.
  type     = "HTTP"
  url_path = "/healthz"

  interval            = 10
  timeout             = 5
  healthy_threshold   = 2
  unhealthy_threshold = 3
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `healthy_threshold` (Number) Consecutive successes before a member counts as healthy (1-10).
- `interval` (Number) Seconds between probes (5-300).
- `lb_id` (String) ID of the load balancer. Changing this forces a new resource to be created.
- `pool_id` (String) ID of the pool to monitor. A pool can have only one monitor. Changing this forces a new resource to be created.
- `timeout` (Number) Seconds to wait for a probe response (5-60).
- `type` (String) Probe type. One of: HTTP, HTTPS, TCP, PING. Changing this forces a new resource to be created.
- `unhealthy_threshold` (Number) Consecutive failures before a member counts as unhealthy (1-10).

### Optional

- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))
- `url_path` (String) Path requested by HTTP and HTTPS probes, e.g. /healthz.

### Read-Only

- `expected_codes` (String) Response codes treated as healthy.
- `health_monitor_id` (String) ID of the monitor on its own, without the load balancer prefix.
- `http_method` (String) HTTP method used by the probe.
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `name` (String) Name assigned by the platform.
- `operating_status` (String) Operating status.
- `provisioning_status` (String) Provisioning status.

<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String)
- `delete` (String)
- `update` (String)

## Behaviour worth knowing

* **A pool can carry only one monitor.** Creating a second one for the same pool is refused by the
  platform.
* **`type` and `pool_id` are fixed at creation.** The timings, the thresholds and `url_path` change
  in place.
* **`url_path` and `expected_codes` apply to HTTP and HTTPS probes only.** A `TCP` or `PING` monitor
  ignores them.

## Timeouts

`create`, `update` and `delete` each default to 15 minutes.

## Import

```shell
# <load-balancer-id>:<health-monitor-id>
terraform import dtcloud_lb_health_monitor.web 3d372446-4c75-4327-9511-98442456162f:9a71c2d8-3f65-4b12-8ad0-6e5c4b9f2a17
```
